html:
On 1 April 2001 the Netherlands became the first country in the world to let couples of the same sex marry. The law had passed both houses of parliament in 2000.

At midnight that day the mayor of Amsterdam, Job Cohen, married four couples. The law gave same-sex couples the same civil marriage as everyone else, including adoption rights within the country. It built on a registered partnership law of 1998.

The Dutch move came out of a long campaign by gay rights groups, part of a movement that grew after the Stonewall riots of 1969. Belgium followed in 2003, then Spain and Canada in 2005, and dozens of countries since. For the wider story see same-sex marriage.
